Senses.Explanation: A Brahmin wanderer is a social label, not one biography. Chan collections use it for distinct case figures: Long-Claw argues that he accepts nothing, while the Black-clan Brahmin is ordered by Shakyamuni to put down what remains after both flowers are released. Fengxue Yanzhao also raises Hanshan’s verse about a Brahmin dying and meeting Yama. The entry therefore keeps the category separate from any one named wanderer.

Senses.Explanation: The Brahma king is a pre-Chan figure whom Chan records place before the Buddha as requester or attendant. The stored witnesses invoke him in ceremonial comparisons and in questions about who initiated or witnessed an assembly; none of these headword cases supports calling him the presenter of the flower.
